cards.card_text: He is a leper He is blind He is lame
cards.verse_text: And he was a mighty man of valor, but he was a leper.
cards.snippet: And he was a mighty man of valor, but he was a leper.

cards.card_text: He asks, “Am I God, killing and giving life, that this man expects me to cure a leper?”
cards.verse_text: When the king of Israel read the letter, he tore his clothes and asked, “Am I God, killing and giving life, that this man expects me to cure a leper?
cards.snippet: …killing and giving life, that this man expects me to cure a leper?

cards.card_text: True or false: King Uzziah stays a leper until the day of his death.
cards.verse_text: So King Uzziah was a leper until the day of his death.
cards.snippet: So King Uzziah was a leper until the day of his death.

cards.card_text: Uzziah rests with his fathers, and the people say, "He was a leper." So where is King Uzziah buried?
cards.verse_text: And Uzziah rested with his fathers and was buried near them in a field of burial that belonged to the kings, for the people said, “He was a leper.” And his son Jotham reigned in his place.
cards.snippet: …that belonged to the kings, for the people said, “He was a leper.” And his son Jotham reigned in his place.

cards.card_text: Heal the sick, raise the dead, cleanse the lepers, drive out demons.

cards.card_text: The report starts like this: the blind receive sight, the lame walk, the lepers are cleansed, the deaf hear, and Jesus is NOT done yet.
